hints: Notice the directions on the ball: weight acts vertically down, cable tension pulls up along the cable, chain tension pulls along the chain, and the small square shows cable perpendicular to chain.
Recall that a body in equilibrium has zero resultant force, so the three force vectors placed head-to-tail must close to form a triangle.
Compare the triangles by checking where the right angle sits and whether each arrowhead joins to the next tail to run continuously round the triangle.
walkthrough: Identify the forces on the ball: weight vertically downward, tension in the cable directed up along the cable away from the ball, and tension in the chain directed along the chain away from the ball.
Use the equilibrium rule: for three coplanar forces in equilibrium the vector sum is zero, so when placed head-to-tail they must form a closed triangle.

Use the geometry from the first diagram: the chain is marked perpendicular to the cable, so in the force triangle the right angle must be between the tension in the cable vector and the tension in the chain vector.
Eliminate the triangles with the right angle between weight and chain tension because they imply a horizontal chain, which contradicts the sloping chain in the question.

Check arrow sense for a continuous loop: weight runs down the vertical side, chain tension must run from the bottom of the weight back toward the cable side, and cable tension must run back up to the start.

Only the triangle with weight down on the right, chain tension sloping up to the left, cable tension sloping up to the top, and the right angle at the cable-chain junction satisfies both geometry and head-to-tail closure. This is option A.

A.explanation: The three arrows form a closed head-to-tail triangle with the right angle between the cable tension and the chain tension, so the resultant is zero for equilibrium.

B.explanation: The tension in the cable arrow points down along the cable instead of up away from the ball, so the arrows do not follow head-to-tail round the triangle.

C.explanation: The right angle is shown between the weight and the chain tension, but the diagram in the question shows the cable perpendicular to the chain.

D.explanation: The right angle is in the wrong place and the cable and chain arrows both point toward the same region, so they do not make a continuous closed loop.
